description: The Federal Agency for Cartography and Geodesy (BKG) sells, through its Geodatenzentrum shop, a Germany-wide set of digital orthophotos. The product page read on 2026-09-28 explains that the surveying administrations of the federal states produce orthophotos, distortion-free and georeferenced aerial images, at 20 centimetre ground resolution, and that BKG merges them across state borders into nationwide DOP20 datasets; it also lists multitemporal RapidEye satellite imagery at 5 metres from 2009, 2012, 2015 and 2017, available only to federal agencies. Coverage is Germany. Access is paid: DOP20 is priced from 2,500 euros, and the RapidEye images are restricted to federal users; the licence terms were not read. Caveats: many federal states publish their own orthophotos free of charge as open data, which may be cheaper for regional work, and flight dates differ between states. It supports exposure and digital twin studies, such as mapping building footprints, roofs and roads for a flood exposure model or checking infrastructure assets against imagery. Related records: BKG's heavy rainfall hazard map and GNSS data centre.
